name: Translations
description: UI texts kept in the database on top of the module dictionaries in code: a language the code does not ship, or a corrected text, live without a deploy or a store release. Read order is database > JSON > English. Rows are per (locale, module, platform, key); platform NULL is shared by web and mobile.
author: Kuray Karaaslan

permissions.name: Read the public UI texts
permissions.description: The languages offered and their stored texts, read by the apps before sign-in.

permissions.name: Read the stored UI texts
permissions.description: System-level: list, summarise and export the texts every tenant reads. Root super-admin only (GLOBAL scope).

permissions.name: Edit the stored UI texts
permissions.description: System-level: save, delete and import the texts every tenant reads. Root super-admin only (GLOBAL scope); audited.

extensions.description: Phase 55: the signal kinds this module emits (the audit actions it owns: the platform's interface texts saved, removed and imported), each attribute with its personal-data class. Read by ai_firewall through its registry; imports only the contract from common.

metadata.label: translation: interface texts saved, removed and imported (phase 55 coverage)

extensionPoints.description: A module whose UI texts are created at run time (the sidebar's renamed items, added workspaces and custom links of shell_menu) names their keys with their English source, so Platform -> Translations lists, counts, exports and imports them like any key and never flags their stored texts as leftovers. Default export: { sources() } implementing TranslationSourceProvider, answering [{ module, key, en }]; `module` must be the contributor's own id and the key must start with it. At most 5000 per provider; a provider that throws is left out of that answer. translation imports nothing of the contributing module.
